ofertaPrecios.titulo: Column “{{columna}}” has prices, not offer mechanics
ofertaPrecios.detalle: That column should carry the offer headline (“2x$299”, “6x4”, “2nd unit at 50%”), but it came with prices. As is, the mechanic can't be built and that price won't be used by anything. Read it as the offer price? If this is the regular export (OFERTA repeats the price on “Precio fijo” rows and carries the percentage on “% Descuento” rows), leave it: the price already comes from the PRECIO column.

rrss.fuenteHint: The mailing PDF ({{mailing}}) or the campaign spreadsheet ({{planilla}})
rrss.arrastraFuente: Drop the mailing or the campaign spreadsheet here
rrss.fuenteUnaUOtra: Only one: either the mailing or the spreadsheet. A new one replaces the previous one, and if you drop several only the first is taken.
rrss.planillaComoSeLee: This is a spreadsheet: CatTi does not look at it, it reads it. It can come in any shape — any column titles, on any row — and CatTi works out what each column is. Then each post is matched to its row by the description and compared against the cell, as is.
rrss.planillaColumnas: The only thing it must have is the product description. Everything else (prices, currency, mechanic, badge texts, dates, alcohol notice) is checked if present, whatever the column is called. What it does not say is not made up: at the end you get the list of what was left unchecked.
rrss.planillaTope: Up to {{max}} products: it is ONE campaign's listing, not the whole catalogue.
rrss.fechaCampana: Campaign dates, as printed on the post
rrss.fechaCampanaVacio: Empty = whatever the mailing says. With a spreadsheet, empty = dates are not checked.

rrss.leyendoPlanillaHint: It is a data file: read whole, no images involved. Takes a second and uses no AI.
